text:
elaine: quick question — running into issues with our .NET client around HttpClient lifetime + Polly retries + streaming responses. anyone bumped into this?

matt: yeah, a couple times. what's the symptom?

elaine: when we enable streaming (ResponseHeadersRead + ReadAsStreamAsync) and have a retry policy, sometimes the first attempt streams fine, but Polly won’t retry on transient 5xx because the request/response stream already got consumed. other times we see socket exhaustion when we create a new HttpClient per request.

sasha: classic two things: 1) don't new up HttpClient per request — use IHttpClientFactory or singleton HttpClient. 2) HttpRequestMessage/HttpContent aren't reusable, so Polly retries can't replay the body unless you buffer or recreate it.

amy: here's a minimal pattern that worked for us: register typed client via AddHttpClient and let DI manage lifetime. For retries, clone the request content if it's a stream, or buffer to MemoryStream for small payloads.

vincent: note re: streaming: if you use `HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead`, you must ensure you fully dispose the response (and the stream) on both success/failure, otherwise connections leak. also prefer SocketsHttpHandler with PooledConnectionLifetime set appropriately.

elaine: any concrete code tips for combining Polly and streaming without buffering the whole payload (we have multi-MB requests sometimes)?

matt: for large request bodies you can't buffer them in memory easily. Two options: 1) retry only idempotent GETs/HEADs and avoid retries for large POSTs, or 2) use a rewindable stream (e.g., FileStream or a custom Stream that can seek) so the HttpContent can be recreated for each attempt.

sasha: sample approach to clone HttpRequestMessage before each Polly attempt: create a factory method that returns a new HttpRequestMessage with the same Method/RequestUri/Headers and a fresh HttpContent. example: 

```csharp
HttpRequestMessage CreateRequest(byte[] bodyBytes) => new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, url)
{
    Content = new ByteArrayContent(bodyBytes)
};

await Policy.Handle<HttpRequestException>()
    .OrResult<HttpResponseMessage>(r => (int)r.StatusCode >= 500)
    .RetryAsync(3, onRetry: (outcome, retryCount) => { /* logging */ })
    .ExecuteAsync(ct => client.SendAsync(CreateRequest(body), HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, ct));
```

sasha: that assumes you can load bodyBytes (maybe from disk or temp file).

ria: another wrinkle: Ensure you're not calling `EnsureSuccessStatusCode()` before you decide to retry, because that throws and can dispose the response. Use Polly predicates on the response status code instead.

amy: for streaming reads, read the stream into a PipeReader or stream copy to destination and close promptly. Example for streaming download: 

```csharp
using var resp = await client.SendAsync(req, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, ct);
if ((int)resp.StatusCode >= 500) return resp; // let Polly decide before reading?
using var stream = await resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(ct);
await stream.CopyToAsync(destinationStream, ct);
```

ci-bot: deploy-bot: noticed elevated 4xx/5xx rates on /v1/stream endpoint 1h ago — correlating with recent SDK change?

vincent: fwiw we fixed a leak by turning off AutomaticDecompression on a specific handler because some servers send chunked encodings that our parser didn't like. small edge case but worth checking.

elaine: thanks. follow-ups: (1) we'll switch to IHttpClientFactory typed client and ensure SocketsHttpHandler pooled settings; (2) add a recommendation to avoid retries for non-idempotent large bodies or require a rewindable stream; (3) update devex docs with examples for ResponseHeadersRead + Polly.

matt: happy to review the docs PR. also add a sample showing how to wrap request creation so it's safe to retry.

sasha: one more gotcha — when using HttpClientFactory, be careful with named clients and handlers ordering if you add DelegatingHandlers for telemetry/retry. handler order matters.

elaine: cool — I'll open a quick RFC and a docs PR with snippets. pinging @matt @sasha for review. thanks all :thumbsup:

matt: :+1:

ria: saved a snippet to our internal snippets repo under devex/dotnet/http-retries.md, I'll link once PR is up.

elaine: great, closing this thread for now.
